'''Kari Jorun Blakkisrud Hag''' (1941–2026) was a Norwegian mathematician known for her research in [[complex analysis]] on [[quasicircle]]s and [[quasiconformal mapping]]s, and for her efforts for gender equality in mathematics. She was a professor of mathematics at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] (NTNU).{{r|ntnu}} With [[Frederick Gehring]] she is the author of the book ''The Ubiquitous Quasidisk'' (American Mathematical Society, 2012).{{r|haissinsky}}

==Education and career==
Hag was originally from [[Eidsvoll]]. She studied at the {{ill|Norwegian School of Education in Trondheim|no|Den allmennvitenskapelige høgskole}}, completing a [[cand.mag.]] in 1963, and then at the [[University of Oslo]], completing a [[cand.real.]] in 1967.{{r|stolav|snl}} Following this, she
earned her doctorate in 1972 from the [[University of Michigan]]. Her dissertation, ''Quasiconformal Boundary Correspondences and Extremal Mappings'', was supervised by Gehring.{{r|mgp}}

After completing her doctorate, she joined the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]] (NTH), which later became part of NTNU.{{r|snl}} She became a full professor at NTNU in 2001, and retired as a professor emerita in 2011.{{r|stolav}}

==Awards and honors==
NTNU gave Hag their gender equality award in 2000, for her efforts to increase the interest of girls in science and mathematics.{{r|likestillingspris}}
In 2018 she was elected as a knight in the [[Order of St. Olav]].{{r|stolav}}
